summary: TLS offload segment-boundary shift causes SSE stream to lose terminal JSON delimiter after path migration
description:
Issue summary: Customer (AcmeDocs) reported reproducible truncated streaming responses when their clients switch network paths (Wi-Fi -> Cellular) while using SSE. The final JSON array terminator or closing object is missing in ~20% of reproductions, leaving the client-side parser hanging.

Impact: Customer reports production users see partial answers or clients that never receive the closing "end" marker for streamed choices; manifests as stuck UI and increased support tickets. Affects enterprise tier; customer needs a reliable streaming experience for their editor feature.

Environment: prod, us-east region, requests proxied through our edge (NGINX w/ TLS offload at CDN provider), fronted by Redwood API gateway, model: redwood-chat-v1 (streaming SSE).

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Open SSE stream to /v1/streams with long output (multi-paragraph).
2) Start on Wi-Fi. After ~3s of tokens, toggle to cellular (iPhone, or use iptables to emulate).
3) Observe stream: intermediate chunks arrive. In failing runs the last JSON chunk containing the terminal metadata and closing array/object is absent; the connection shows a short TLS-close from the CDN and the downstream SSE connection is left half-closed.

Observed behavior: Final closing JSON token ("event: done" + closing JSON) not received by client; server-side logs show the runtime emitted the terminal frame and then a short TLS record with FIN, but edge traces indicate the TLS record was split by TLS offload/inspector and reassembled differently by the CDN, leading to the closing delimiter being delivered in a separate segment that is dropped/reordered during the path migration.

Expected behavior: All stream terminal markers and closing JSON should reliably reach client even across network handoffs; stream reconnect/resume should preserve final marker or emit an explicit "terminal-missing" diagnostic if lost.

Attachments/logs: Provided below are trimmed excerpts from customer and edge traces (timestamps redacted):
- Client console: "SSE open, received chunk id=341, chunk id=342, ... hung"
- Edge proxy trace (hex of TLS record lengths): [0x16/0x03/0x03 len=2048] -> [0x16/0x03/0x03 len=128] -> (path-migrate) -> [0x17/0x03/0x03 len=24]
- Server runtime emit log: "choice_id=abc123 emitted final_event=done bytes=112"
- Upstream ack: "tcp retransmit, segment out of order"

Notes: Customer supplied PCAP showing that the closing JSON (final 112 bytes) is split across two TLS records and the CDN's TLS termination appears to coalesce different upstream segments when migrating the connection, resulting in a dropped tail when the client socket is rotated.

Priority justification: P1 because enterprise customer production UX affected and reproducer provided.
investigation_notes: 03-01: Support triaged with AcmeDocs. Initial hypothesis: proxy idle/keepalive teardown during path migration (similar to SUP-310999 patterns) but customer trace shows explicit TLS record boundary change.

03-01: SRE obtained edge NGINX + CDN termination logs; observed short TLS close immediately after runtime reported final emit. CDN records show two TLS records for the final payload that land across the path migration window.

03-02: Reproduced internally using a network-path-migration script (iperf+tc+ip rule) against staging with identical edge config; observed ~18% failure where final chunk not delivered to client-side SSE parser.

03-02: Instrumented runtime to include 'terminal-seq' tokens in final emit and added per-chunk sequence numbers; server sees final chunk emitted and acked by upstream TCP, but downstream SSE socket reports half-close before final delimiter reaches app layer.

03-02: Hypothesis refined: TLS offload device at CDN re-segments or coalesces TLS records and during path migration the CDN's socket handoff drops the last small record (common failure when 0-RTT or early-data path migration is enabled).
03-02: Correlation: failures cluster when final payload size < 256 bytes and when path change occurs within 1-2 RTTs after final emit.

03-03: Discussed mitigation: force runtime to send explicit keepalive/flush + larger trailing padding so terminal delimiter sits in an earlier/larger TLS record; or make the streaming protocol emit a separate guaranteed-final 'end-of-stream' event on reconnect if missing.
03-03: Linked to PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2291 (add terminal padding / explicit terminal marker) for testing; engineering to validate in staging with CDN offload enabled.
resolution_notes:
Workaround (short-term): Engineering released a staging build that appends a 512-byte padding block to the final SSE chunk so it is coalesced into a larger TLS record less likely to be dropped by CDN offload. Customer validated in their environment; failure rate dropped from ~18% to <1% in reproducer runs.

Planned permanent fix: (1) Add explicit durable terminal handshake: when client reconnects after an interrupted SSE, the runtime will return an explicit "terminal-missing" diagnostic and a pointer to fetch the final delta via REST. (2) Work with CDN partners to disable aggressive TLS early-data coalescing on streaming routes and add tests for segment boundary behavior. (3) Upstream runtime change (PR #2291) to optionally pad final chunk and add sequence numbers for integrity checks.

Rollout notes: Hotfix padding enabled behind a feature flag for affected enterprise customers. Will roll out to additional customers after partner config validation and synthetic test coverage added.
